endorsements.quote: Among these, the strengthening of democratic governance structures is essential, including ethical and technical committees that incorporate the social participation of health councils and civil society, with the aim of transparently auditing the functioning and impacts of algorithms used in SUS 23 , 46 .

It is also essential to invest in data infrastructure and critical education, ensuring the quality, interoperability, and security of information while promoting algorithmic literacy so that professionals and managers can interpret, question, and apply results in a qualified manner 17 .

Models trained with foreign or generic datasets, without local validation, may produce ineffective or even harmful applications within SUS, thereby compromising the equity and effectiveness of health actions 42 .

unlisted_practices: Mandate rigorous local validation before implementing any AI technology to ensure suitability to the local epidemiological and social context.
Foster technological sovereignty by developing national algorithms and prioritizing open-source software to reduce external dependence.
Invest in data infrastructure to ensure quality, interoperability, and security of health information.
Engage affected communities and conduct continuous auditing and intergroup validation when using sensitive variables such as race and ethnicity.
Use the PAHO institutional readiness assessment tool to evaluate readiness for AI adoption in public health.

screen.reason: Theoretical-analytical commentary discussing the ethical implications, governance, and potential for integrating AI into the Brazilian public health system (SUS).
